key_concepts: Observation using the five senses helps gather accurate and reliable information
Scientific investigations produce evidence that answers questions and solves problems
The scientific method is a systematic way of testing ideas and reporting results
A key component of the scientific method is that experiments must be replicable by anyone
Identifying the problem begins with a question or problem arising from observation
Gathering information about the problem involves background research and citing sources
A hypothesis is an educated guess that gives a testable explanation
A good hypothesis allows a prediction often phrased as an if-then statement
An experiment is a controlled scientific study of specific variables
A fair test changes only one factor at a time
The independent variable is manipulated while the dependent variable responds
Controlled variables are kept the same so they do not influence results
